bib.title: Estimating or Propagating Gradients Through Stochastic Neurons for Conditional Computation

question: How can the gradient of a loss be estimated or propagated through stochastic or hard-threshold neurons, so that sparse gating units can be trained for conditional computation?
hypothesis: Noise-injected and estimator-based stochastic units can be trained well enough to gate computation, giving sparse activations at little cost in accuracy.
contributions: Compare four families of gradient estimators for stochastic/non-smooth neurons
Introduce the STS (stochastic times smooth) unit
Prove an unbiased minimum-variance estimator for stochastic binary neurons (REINFORCE special case)
Name and test the straight-through estimator
Small-scale conditional computation experiment on MNIST

method.summary: Four estimators (noisy rectifier, STS, unbiased stochastic-binary-neuron estimator, straight-through) are used to train a gater network that multiplies a 2000-unit linear expert layer, with 10% target sparsity, on MNIST. Compared with rectifier and sigmoid baselines.
method.task: MNIST classification with a conditional computation (gated) hidden layer

models.name: Gater + expert conditional layer
models.architecture: 4 affine transforms; gater: input -> 400 tanh hidden -> 2000 gating units; expert: linear 2000 hidden units; elementwise product; affine + softmax over 10 classes

other.gating nonlinearities: Noisy Rectifier, STS, Stochastic Binary Neuron, Straight-through, non-noisy rectifier

models.name: Baseline Sigmoid / Sigmoid+Noise
models.architecture: gater sigmoid output, tanh hidden, no sparsity constraint, 200 output units for gater and main part; Sigmoid+Noise adds Gaussian noise in training

training.objective: classification loss plus sparsity penalty: KL(s||p) with lambda for sigmoids (mini-batch mean activation, s=0.1), L1 with adaptive lambda for rectifiers
training.optimizer: inferred: SGD with momentum (momentum used for STS; little/no effect for ST and Noisy Rectifier, negative for SBN)
training.batch_size: inferred: 32 (sparsity statistics computed over mini-batch of 32 propagations)
training.regularisation: max-norm 2 on incoming weights (best in most cases); sparsity penalty; Beta noise at sigmoid input for STS

other.STS Beta noise: beta ~40.1 best, tried 1.1, 2.6, 5.1, 10.1, 20.1, 40.1, 80.1, 160.1; alpha set so mode = 0.1; mean replaces noise at test
other.lambda adaptation: increase when effective sparsity > s+0.01, reduce when < s-0.01
other.test-time: deterministic; threshold optimised to give 10% ones

metrics.name: validation/test classification error
metrics.definition: error on MNIST valid/test; stochastic models evaluated with deterministic counterpart and optimised threshold

eval.protocol: single reported run per method; no seeds or variance given; MNIST split sizes not stated

evidence.quote: Experiments are performed with a gater of 400 hidden units and 2000 output units.

results.claim: Straight-through gater gave the best validation error among all gaters.
results.table: Figure 2 table, row Straight-through, column valid

results.claim: Straight-through gater gave the best test error.
results.quote: Another surprise is the good performance of the straight-through units, which provided the best validation and test error, and are very simple to implement.

results.note: Valid 1.52 vs baseline rectifier 1.66; test is worse than baseline though the text says noisy gater gave better results

results.table: Figure 2 table, row Stoch. Binary Neuron, column test

results.claim: Gater with 10% sparsity cuts main-path cost from O(N^2) to O(alpha N^2), gater costs O(MN).
results.quote: the gater's bottleneck layer has size M ≪N, then computing the gater output is O(MN), which can reduce the main path computations from O(N 2) to O(αN 2).

results.claim: Unbiased estimator for stochastic binary neurons: (h - sigm(a)) * L, with centred minimum-variance baseline.
Straight-through estimator is biased but has the right sign for a single layer; works better without multiplying by sigmoid derivative.
results.quote: It is clearly a biased estimator, but when considering a single layer of neurons, it has the right sign (this is not guaranteed anymore when back-propagating through more hidden layers).

limits: Small-scale: one MNIST architecture, one conditional layer, stacking not attempted
No actual runtime savings measured, only expected from sparsity
Single-run numbers, no variance, MNIST splits and epochs not given
STE is a heuristic, biased; sign guarantee fails across multiple layers
Noisy rectifier test error (1.87) is worse than non-noisy baseline rectifier (1.60) despite the conclusion's claim

terms.definition: back-propagate through the hard threshold function as if it had been the identity function
Stochastic Times Smooth: p=sigm(a), b~Binomial(sqrt p), h=b/sqrt p

lineage.note: unbiased estimator is a special case
perturbation estimator, biased unless perturbations small
